itens.titulo: JPMorgan Misses Q3 Estimates, but Dimon’s Buyback Cut Is the Bigger Story
itens.descricao: JPMorgan Misses Q3 Estimates, but Dimon’s Buyback Cut Is the Bigger Story Yahoo Finance
trechos: JPMorgan Chase (JPM:NYSE) missed Wall Street's third-quarter estimates on Tuesday, October 13, a rare stumble for the largest US bank.
It reported earnings of $5.57 per share against a $5.90 consensus, and managed revenue of $50.9 billion fell short of the roughly $51.3 billion analysts expected.
After drifting between small gains and losses before the bell, JPM shares were up about 1% in early trading, near $338.
JPMorgan booked $658 million of pretax losses on investment securities, worth $0.18 a share.
Without it, EPS was $5.75 (still a miss).
Fixed-income markets revenue fell 4% from a year earlier to $5.4 billion, its first decline in more than two years.
Equities trading jumped 49% to $5.0 billion, investment banking fees rose 14%, and net income still climbed 6% to $15.3 billion.

The Lending Engine Is Speeding Up Net interest income (what JPMorgan earns on loans and securities after paying depositors) is the bank's biggest profit engine, and it reached $27.0 billion this quarter.

itens.descricao: How Has Chevron's Story Changed? Yahoo Finance
trechos: Chevron (CVX) stock is currently priced at 20.6 times earnings, compared with 21.9 for the S&P 500.
During its fiscal 2024 earnings calls, management emphasized the net debt ratio.
On the fiscal Q2 2026 call held on July 31, 2026, management placed that figure at 0.6 times.
On the fiscal Q3 2024 call, executives noted that Chevron finished the quarter with a net debt ratio under 12%.
One call later, they reported a ratio of 10% for the end of 2024.
During the fiscal Q4 2025 call in January 2026, executives said they moved toward the measures used by rating agencies.
Chevron's Debt Is Small And Has Been Cut Chevron's debt amounts to 8.7% of the company's market value, compared with 21% for the S&P 500.
Management noted on the fiscal Q2 2026 call that Chevron reduced debt by more than $8 billion in the second quarter.

itens.titulo: Between Amazon and Alphabet One’s Gotten Much More Bang for Their 200 Billion Bucks
itens.descricao: Between Amazon and Alphabet One’s Gotten Much More Bang for Their 200 Billion Bucks Yahoo Finance
trechos: Quick Read - Google Cloud (GOOGL) grew 82% versus AWS's (AMZN) 37%, yet the faster grower trades at a cheaper 23x forward earnings than Amazon's 24x.
- Alphabet suspended buybacks, nearly doubled long-term debt to $98 billion, and turned quarterly free cash flow negative to fund its AI buildout.
- Alphabet shares climbed 49% over the past year versus Amazon's 20%, with nearly 90% of Fortune 100 companies already using Gemini Enterprise.
Alphabet guided 2026 capex of $175 billion to $185 billion, and Amazon plans roughly $200 billion.
Google Cloud Sprints While AWS Leans on Scale Google Cloud revenue jumped 82% to $24.77 billion, up from 63% growth in Q1.
CEO Sundar Pichai noted that nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 now use Gemini Enterprise.
Search and other revenue still grew 17%, so AI features appear to be feeding the core ad engine.
AWS grew 36.7% to $42.2 billion, its fastest pace in 18 quarters, and runs at a $169 billion annualized rate.
